1. The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite and is about one-quarter the diameter of Earth, making it the fifth-largest moon in the solar system relative to its planet's size.
2. The same side of the Moon always faces Earth because it is tidally locked, meaning its orbital period matches its rotation period (about 27.3 days).
3. The Moon has no significant atmosphere, which causes extreme temperature swings—from about 127°C (260°F) during the day to -173°C (-280°F) at night.
